parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/app.module.ts is a NestJS root module. It falls in the presentation layer through the **/*.module.ts pattern. Its only job is to wire modules together: it imports ConfigModule, TypeOrmModule and DeliveryModule and declares AppModule with no methods. It holds no business rules and no request handling. It has no queries, repositories or other persistence logic, only module registration. TypeOrmModule.forRoot does pass connection settings (host, port, credentials, synchronize, logging) and an entity list. You could argue those settings belong in an infrastructure config provider. Still, a NestJS module file is meant to register framework modules, and these values come from config() rather than being hardcoded. No ADR prose was given that would forbid this. The file therefore does not carry another layer's responsibility as the rubric defines it. That inline database setup is the only borderline point, so confidence is moderate.
